I haven't been using this program for a very long time.
It feels intuitive, designed for what it was meant - pixel arts and less demanding vector graphics.

I haven't tested high details vector graphics yet (mostly using symmetric simple shapes anyway, so there was no reason for me to add myself more work).

There are some bugs that I desire to share with the developers. For example the APNG export animation mode is broken. The files contain badly written data in hex code, this may work in firefox, but in chrome will not. I have tested it using other tools - they work fine.

Beside that, the animations mode is really nice, it may have a slight issue. The preview window is too small for some irregular graphics. If you design a very long sidebar or wide element which proportions are not "regular" or "common" then the window may not be as easy to use. 

The outlines functionality is a bit buggy when scaled. It sometimes isn't processed by the scaling algorithm and sometimes gets utterly broken. Beside that - I really like it. The grids... the grids are awesome, that's one of the best functionalities in this program.

You can create fancy simple pictures, graphics with irregular shapes. You can choose triangles, rhombs, isometric "rhombs", hexagonal shapes, shards.

 What I sometimes dislike is that this program lacks a function of "subdividing". Something like in Blender yeah? It could be theoretically done quite easily, you just increase a color size in specific area into a larger "triangle" or alike figure and then the same shape is represented with more of "virtual pixels".

It isn't written (the feature) I believe. The colors, the effects (a nice feature), the gloom and basically the quickness of the program are nice. It is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ free, doesn't contain "please login in else your mother will die" type of ♥♥♥♥, is responsive and I generally had veryyyy goooddd feelings about it after trying to use ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for the third time with only headache being the product of my work ...

The grid perfectly matches the area. That's what I find CRUCIAL, you can't draw something if the grid doesn't symmetrically connect to the sides of the canvas. Yeah, if you're a normie then sure, you can even paint with chicken nuggets dipped in szechuan sauce, the point is that some people want to make THE SAME IN SIZE textures, so every block/rectangle are of the same size and I don't mean the output size, because you can (that's a nice feature) scale it in vector graphics mode easily.

The issue normally arises when you want to use ♥♥♥♥-tools like Inkscape where the grid never matches the drawing area. You end up with the grid being larger/smaller than the "page" (in the sense that the triangles/rectangles don't precisely connect with the edges of the page) and thus you can't set up a for example 48x48 size as your "base" size and then create the same sized blocks (for minecraft, website projects, pixel arts, whatever really).

This program does it. I really like those things. I hope for developers to fix some of the mentioned issues and then it will be a STRONG 8/10. It could contain some more export options, perhaps gloom effect put into individual tiles/hexels.

For the price (at least the discounted price) it does the job pretty well and I am very happy to have bought it.
